result.title: MemLife: Curating and Reasoning over Long-Term Egocentric Video Memories
result.summary: Long-term egocentric video enables personalized AI assistants to reason about daily life. However, as video histories grow to hundreds of hours spanning months or years, reprocessing raw clips for every query becomes computationally prohibitive. Memory systems offer a scalable alternative by compacting videos into text representations, but often fail on practical benchmarks: either the memory does not preserve key evidence, or the retriever fails to locate relevant entries due to retrieval competition in growing search spaces. To address these challenges, we introduce MemLife, a multimodal memory system that constructs entity-grounded, first-person text episodes and retrieves them via a time-indexed agentic reader. Without training or query-time video access, MemLife improves over the strongest training-free baseline by 4.6--12.0% across four long-horizon benchmarks. To further improve memory quality, we propose MemOpt, a reinforcement learning framework that optimizes the memory writer to produce faithful, informative, and retrievable memories. MemOpt consistently improves MemLife by 2.7--5.0% across different video and question distributions, with gains that generalize across writer and reader backbones and memory systems.

AI.brief_summary: MemLife 面向长时自我中心视频，将数百小时视频压缩为实体锚定、第一人称的文本记忆片段，并用时间索引的 agentic reader 检索；配套 MemOpt 以强化学习优化记忆写入器，使记忆更忠实、信息量更高且更易检索，在四个长时基准上优于免训练基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 的「是否保留任务必要视觉证据」「证据筛选与检索、缓存」问题直接相关，其文本记忆压缩造成的细节与几何信息损失、以及写入器与检索器间的贡献分配，可供核查潜在的 latent 记忆/状态设计借鉴。
